subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that cos⁴(π/8) + cos⁴(3π/8) + cos⁴(5π/8) + cos⁴(7π/8) = 3/2.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reduce the four angles to two
steps.margin_note: Note the minus signs on two of the reductions. They matter for the working and vanish at the fourth power — say so rather than dropping them silently.

recall.must_convey: That the allied-angle reductions are done, including the two that carry a minus sign.
accept: reduce the angles, two of them come out negative but they are raised to the fourth power
cos five pi by eight is minus sin pi by eight and cos seven pi by eight is minus cos pi by eight
use allied angles and keep the minus signs
rendu terms minus vasthai kani fourth power kabatti poddu
the reductions give sin and cos of pi by eight with signs

steps.why: A negative raised to an even power is positive, so the minus signs disappear — but writing them down is what shows the reduction was done properly.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus signs without saying why they do not matter.
Assuming the answer must differ from the sin⁴ version because of the signs.
steps.memory_tip: Two reductions come out NEGATIVE. Say so — the signs vanish only at the fourth power.

steps.label: Group and use a² + b²
steps.margin_note: First mark. The fourth power makes both minus signs positive, so the expression is 2[sin⁴ + cos⁴] — identical to the sin⁴ version from here on.

lines.text: Put these in; a fourth power removes the minus:

recall.must_convey: That the fourth powers remove the minus signs, and the same a² + b² = (a+b)² − 2ab identity is applied.
accept: the fourth powers remove the signs so it becomes two times sin fourth plus cos fourth, same as the twin
group and apply the same algebraic identity
minus to the fourth is plus so the expression matches the other question
fourth power kabatti signs poyi, twin lanti same expression vasthundi
apply a squared plus b squared identity

steps.why: From this line onward this question and the sin⁴ version are word for word identical, so the rest of the working is the same on both.
common_mistakes: Carrying the minus signs into the fourth powers.
steps.memory_tip: (−x)⁴ = x⁴, so the four terms become 2[sin⁴ + cos⁴], then a² + b² = (a+b)² − 2ab on the squares.

steps.label: Turn the product into sin(π/4)
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Identical finish to the sin⁴ version, and the same answer.

lines.text: and 4 sin²θ cos²θ = (2 sin θ cos θ)²:

recall.must_convey: That the product becomes sin²(π/4) = 1/2, giving 3/2 — the same answer as the sin⁴ version.
accept: the product becomes sin pi by four squared which is a half so the answer is three by two
same finish as the other question, three halves
two minus a half is three by two
sin pi by four square half, so three by two
the answer is three by two, same as the twin

steps.why: This question and the sin⁴ version both give 3/2 because after reduction they are the same sum. Getting a different answer means a reduction went wrong.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to square the bracket, so 2 sin(π/8) cos(π/8) is used in place of sin²(π/4).
steps.memory_tip: 4sin²cos² is (2 sin cos)² = sin²(π/4) = 1/2, so the answer is 2 − 1/2.

insider_note: Reduce all four angles to π/8 first; the two minus signs vanish under a fourth power. Then a⁴ + b⁴ needs (a²+b²)² − 2a²b², and 2 sin cos = sin(π/4) finishes it.
